title: Graded Admission Controller and Regional Fallback Runbook for Quota Continuity
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Design and implement a graded admission controller plus a region-aware fallback protocol to maintain SLOs during limiter outages, cross-region congestion, and sudden tenant bursts. This ticket covers design decisions, telemetry and SLO mapping, implementation tasks, chaos testing, and a stepwise rollout plan with rollback criteria. Goal: keep p95 latency and availability SLOs within target for tiered customers while gracefully shedding load and preserving fairness when quota stores or admission services degrade.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New admission controller can operate in three graded modes (Green/Degraded/Critical) with deterministic token accounting. 2) Regional fallback automatically routes traffic to a compatible admission tier in another region within 10s when local lease sync fails. 3) Rollout shows <5% additional user-level errors for P1 customers in canary region, and no regression for P0. 4) Telemetry surfaces per-tenant effective admission rate, queued requests, and grace-drain events. 5) Integration tests and chaos scenarios pass in staging and pre-prod.
design_summary: We will implement a multilayer admission system: (A) local admission cache with lease-backed token reservoir (short-lived, eventually consistent), (B) graded admission states that reduce allowed concurrency and per-second throughput in measured steps, and (C) a cross-region fallback broker that accepts signed short-lived leases to serve as temporary quota authority. Circuit breakers will be co-located with the admission logic and follow hysteresis windows tied to SLO-derived thresholds. Fairness is implemented with weighted deficit round-robin in the admission hot-path to preserve tenant proportions under shedding.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Strong consistency for quotas would increase tail latency; we choose eventual/lease semantics to favor availability and fast admission decisions.
- Graded shedding preserves high-priority tenants but may increase tail latency for lower tiers; we will tune weights and implement short soft-stops to avoid starvation.
- Cross-region fallback introduces additional egress and complexity; fallback leases are short (30s) and require signed proof to avoid double-spend.
- Circuit breakers are conservative: open only after multiple signals (quota store latency, admission error rate, and SLO drift) to reduce flapping.
implementation_notes: 1) Admission service exposes /admit and /lease endpoints. 2) Local reservoir keeps windowed counters and an optimistic remaining-tokens estimate. 3) On token-store timeouts, admission switches to Degraded mode and consults regional broker. 4) Circuit-breaker state persisted in RAFT-backed local store for quick recovery. 5) Weighted DRR scheduler implemented in C++ hot-path with fallback to Go path for rare slow cases.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for reservoir math and DRR scheduler.
- Integration tests simulating token-store latency and leader kill.
- Chaos scenarios: region partition, token-store fail-stop, and burst spike.
- Staging canary with 5% of production traffic; realtime dashboards to monitor p95 latency and error budget burn.
- Long-running soak test to validate fairness over 24h bursts.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind org-level gate. 2) Deploy admission service to staging and run integration suite. 3) Canary rollout to eu-west-1 with 5% of traffic for 48h. 4) If stable, increase to 25% for 72h while monitoring error budget and tenant fairness signals. 5) Full global rollout in waves per region. 6) Post-mortem and tuning window after 2 weeks.
rollback_criteria:
- P0 error rate increases >1% absolute or p95 latency regresses >15% compared to baseline in canary.
- Unbounded increase in queued requests (>10x baseline) for any tenant.
- Any data-inconsistency events observed (double-charge / lease overlap).
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: admission.mode (Green/Degraded/Critical), per-tenant admitted_rps, per-tenant queued_count, lease_miss_rate, fallback_activation_count, circuit_open_count. Dashboards: SLO health, fairness heatmap, regional fallback map. Alerts: fallback_activation_rate > 1/min for >5m, lease_miss_rate > 0.5% sustained 10m, circuit_open_count > 3 in 5m.
security_and_compliance: Signed short-lived region leases use KMS-backed keys; all fallback requests authenticated via mTLS. Audit logs record lease grants and fallback activations for compliance. Security review required prior to GA.
